body: Hm, how do you access the `MyApplication` instance? It seems that resteasy extension does not suppor injecting `javax.ws.rs.core.Application` subclasses into resources via `@Context`... @geoand knows a way more about JAX-RS in quarkus though ;-) ...

`quarkus-resteasy` intializes `MyApplication`. However, with Quarkus 2.x this seems to happen before ARC/CDI is set up, hence `@Inject MyBean myBean;` does not work (ie. `myBean` is null inside `getClasses`). This worked ok on 1.6.1.
@mkouba Update: the same issue also happens with 1.13.x, meaning the regression wasn't introduced with 2.x as I stated above. The latest version that works for me is 12.2.Final.

issue.title: Disallow the use of @Inject in JAX-RS Application classes
issue.body:
This did not work anyway, so it probably makes sense to
disallow it completely

Closes: #22277

issue.title: Properly handle `@ApplicationPath` and `Application` in RESTEasy Classic
issue.body:
`@ApplicationPath` is only taken into account for the single `Application` class that is selected (if any).

- Fixes: #42963
